title: On the Maldacena-Shenker-Stanford chaos bound in black hole spacetimes: Saturation, apparent violations, and their geometric origin
summary: Reported violations of the Maldacena-Shenker-Stanford (MSS) chaos bound in black hole spacetimes raise the question of whether they reflect a genuine breakdown, a feature of particular geometries, or a limitation of the probe used to test the bound. We show that the violations are apparent and arise predominantly in the near-extremal regime, where the black hole develops an $AdS_2\times S^2$ throat, the surface gravity becomes parametrically small, while the Lyapunov exponent of an orbit separated from the throat remains nonzero.
